title: Filling a drilled hole in a ceramic tile
subtitle: Fill an unwanted drilled fixings hole in a glazed wall tile with colour-matched filler or epoxy
excerpt: How to fill a redundant drilled hole in a ceramic wall tile. Covers cleaning the hole, choosing between epoxy filler and tile repair compound, matching the colour, and finishing flush.
sourceNotes: UK trade practice for tile repair.

glossaryTerms.definition: A filler made by mixing a resin and a hardener in equal parts. Once mixed, it sets hard and bonds to glass, ceramics, and metal. The main advantage over single-component fillers is that it does not shrink as it cures, giving a flush fill in a single application. Set time is typically 30 to 60 minutes at room temperature.

or a tile repair compound. Clean the hole, pack the filler flush, and match the glaze colour if needed. The repair is nearly invisible on a plain tile.

Pick out any loose plaster dust and debris from the hole with a pin or narrow implement. Wipe the tile face and the inside of the hole with isopropyl alcohol (or a small amount of methylated spirit on a cotton bud) to degrease the surface. The filler will not bond to a dusty or greasy surface.

For holes up to about 6 mm (a standard wall plug drill size), two-part epoxy filler works well. Mix a small amount on a scrap of card following the ratio on the pack, usually equal lengths of resin and hardener. Work quickly: the pot life once mixed is typically 5 to 10 minutes. For a white or near-white tile, the filler may be an acceptable colour match as supplied. If the tile is coloured, buy a specialist tile repair kit that includes small pots of paint for colour matching.
Pack the hole and finish flush

Pack the filler firmly into the hole with the tip of the filling knife, slightly overfilling so the filler is just proud of the tile surface. Apply a small piece of masking tape over the filled hole with a pinhole in the centre to prevent the filler mounding on the glaze face. Once the filler has hardened (30 to 60 minutes for most two-part epoxy), remove the tape and file or sand the fill flush with a sanding block using a very fine (240 grit) abrasive. Sand carefully to avoid scratching the tile glaze.

If the cured filler does not match the tile colour, apply a small dot of matching paint (from the tile repair kit, or a touch of enamel model paint) with a fine artist's brush. On white tiles the sanded filler is usually close enough not to need painting.

attrs.symptom: Filler falls out of the hole within a week
attrs.cause: The hole was not cleaned before filling, or single-component filler was used in a wet area where it stayed soft.
attrs.fix: Use two-part epoxy filler in wet areas. Clean the hole thoroughly and allow it to dry before refilling.

attrs.symptom: Sanding the filler flush scratched the tile glaze
attrs.cause: Too coarse an abrasive used when sanding, or the filler was sanded before fully cured.
attrs.fix: Allow the filler to cure fully before sanding. Use 320 grit or finer abrasive and sand in small, gentle circles.
